# Ronnie Sheth, SENEN Group CEO：为什么现在是企业AI‘务实’的时候
2026年2月3日
![](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/RS_screenshot_03_02-1024x702.png)
在你开始AI之旅之前，一定要检查你的数据状态——因为如果有一件事可能会让你的船沉没，那就是数据质量。
Gartner估计，低质量的数据每年给组织带来的浪费资源和失去机会的成本平均为[$12.9百万](https://www.forbes.com/councils/forbescommunicationscouncil/2025/10/22/the-real-cost-of-bad-data-how-it-silently-undermines-pricing-and-growth/)。这是坏消息。好消息是，组织越来越意识到其数据质量的重要性——并且不太可能落入这个陷阱。
这是SENEN Group首席执行官Ronnie Sheth的观点。该公司专注于数据和AI咨询、运营化和素养，Sheth指出她从“还是个公司婴儿”时就开始涉足数据和AI领域，因此她的观点背后有大量的实际经验。也有很多成功案例；Sheth指出，她的公司有99.99%的客户重复率。
“如果我非常务实的话，我发现的一件事是公司在准备好之前就急于采用AI，”Sheth说。她指出，公司会有高管指示他们采用AI，但没有相应的蓝图或路线图。结果可能是令人印象深刻的用户数量，但没有任何可衡量的结果来支持。
甚至在2024年，Sheth还看到许多组织因为他们的数据‘根本不在需要的地方’而苦苦挣扎。“差得远呢，”她补充道。现在，对话变得更加务实和战略化。公司意识到了这一点，并首先来找SENEN Group寻求数据方面的帮助，而不是立即想要采用AI。
“当这样的公司来找我们时，首先要做的就是修复他们的数据，”Sheth说。“接下来要做的是构建他们的AI模型。他们在为任何后续的AI项目打下坚实的基础。
“一旦他们修复了数据，他们可以随心所欲地构建尽可能多的AI模型，并拥有尽可能多的AI解决方案，他们会得到准确的输出，因为他们现在有了坚实的基础，”Sheth补充道。
凭借广泛而深入的专业知识，SENEN Group使组织能够纠正方向。Sheth举了一个客户的例子，该客户来找他们希望进行数据治理计划。最终，他们需要的是数据策略——为什么以及如何，他们试图用数据实现什么目标——然后加入治理并提供一个运营模式的路线图。“他们已经从原始数据转向描述性分析，再转向预测性分析，现在我们实际上正在为他们制定AI策略，”Sheth说。
正是这种态度和对务实举措的需求将成为Sheth本周在伦敦举行的AI & Big Data Expo Global上讨论的核心。“现在是时候让AI变得务实了，特别是企业AI的采用，而不是想着‘看，我们要创新，我们要做试点，我们要实验，’”Sheth说。“现在不是做这些的时候。现在是时候变得务实，让AI产生价值。今年是企业在这一方面行动的时候。”

# [Ronnie Sheth, CEO, SENEN Group: Why now is the time for enterprise AI to ‘get practical’](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/news/ronnie-sheth-ceo-senen-group-why-now-is-the-time-for-enterprise-ai-to-get-practical/)
February 3, 2026
![](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/RS_screenshot_03_02-1024x702.png)
Share this story:
Categories:
## [Artificial Intelligence](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/categories/artificial-intelligence/)  [TechEx Events](https://www.artificialintelligence-news.com/categories/techex-events/)
Before you set sail on your AI journey, always check the state of your data – because if there is one thing likely to sink your ship, it is data quality.
Gartner estimates that poor data quality costs organisations an average of [$12.9 million each year](https://www.forbes.com/councils/forbescommunicationscouncil/2025/10/22/the-real-cost-of-bad-data-how-it-silently-undermines-pricing-and-growth/) in wasted resources and lost opportunities. That’s the bad news. The good news is that organisations are increasingly understanding the importance of their data quality – and less likely to fall into this trap.
That’s the view of Ronnie Sheth, CEO of AI strategy, execution and governance firm [SENEN Group](https://senengroup.com/). The company focuses on data and AI advisory, operationalisation and literacy, and Sheth notes she has been in the data and AI space ‘ever since \[she\] was a corporate baby’, so there is plenty of real-world experience behind the viewpoint. There is also plenty of success; Sheth notes that her company has a 99.99% client repeat rate.
“If I were to be very practical, the one thing I’ve noticed is companies jump into adopting AI before they’re ready,” says Sheth. Companies, she notes, will have an executive direction insisting they adopt AI, but without a blueprint or roadmap to accompany it. The result may be impressive user numbers, but with no measurable outcome to back anything up.
Even as recently as 2024, Sheth saw many organisations struggling because their data was ‘nowhere where it needed to be.’ “Not even close,” she adds. Now, the conversation has turned more practical and strategic. Companies are realising this, and coming to SENEN Group initially to get help with their data, rather than wanting to adopt AI immediately.
“When companies like that come to us, the first course of order is really fixing their data,” says Sheth. “The next course of order is getting to their AI model. They are building a strong foundation for any AI initiative that comes after that.
“Once they fix their data, they can build as many AI models as they want, and they can have as many AI solutions as they want, and they will get accurate outputs because now they have a strong foundation,” Sheth adds.
With breadth and depth in expertise, SENEN Group allows organisations to right their course. Sheth notes the example of one customer who came to them wanting a data governance initiative. Ultimately, it was the data strategy which was needed – the why and how, the outcomes of what they were trying to do with their data – before adding in governance and providing a roadmap for an operating model. “They’ve moved from raw data to descriptive analytics, moving into predictive analytics, and now we’re actually setting up an AI strategy for them,” says Sheth.
It is this attitude and requirement for practical initiatives which will be the cornerstone of Sheth’s discussion at AI & Big Data Expo Global in London this week. “Now would be the time to get practical with AI, especially enterprise AI adoption, and not think about ‘look, we’re going to innovate, we’re going to do pilots, we’re going to experiment,’” says Sheth. “Now is not the time to do that. Now is the time to get practical, to get AI to value. This is the year to do that in the enterprise.”
